properties.name: A gap put to the user arrives with the agent's recommendation — recommending is not deciding
properties.statement:
When reflow2 puts a gap to the user, the agent's READING of it travels with the question: what it would do and why, and what would change that answer. The user still decides; the agent stops pretending it has no view.

THE READING HAS A SHAPE, AND THE SHAPE IS PART OF THE REQUIREMENT — added 2026-07-31 on Anthony's word after the pattern was used on him for the five standing gaps: "I really like when I say something like 'go through the decisions I need to make... put them in plain and simple english and offer a recommendation' and then you give me the options to select with your recommended choice on top. I believe there is already a proposed idea... but I really like this process (I think other users will really like this process also), so I'd either like to update the proposed req or cap or backlog item to CEMENT THIS BEHAVIOR."

Three obligations, and they are separable:

(1) THE OPTIONS ARE SELECTABLE, not buried in prose. The user picks rather than composing a reply. Prose that describes three courses of action still leaves them to name one; a list they can choose from does not.

(2) THE RECOMMENDATION COMES FIRST and is marked as such. Position carries meaning: an unordered menu makes the user infer which the agent favours, which is the analysis req:no-se-knowledge exists to spare them. Marking it also makes an overrule VISIBLE — the user knows they are departing from the agent's view, which is the precondition for the finding below.

(3) EVERY OPTION STILL CARRIES ITS CONSEQUENCE, including the ones not recommended. A list of bare labels is worse than prose, because it looks complete while withholding what each choice costs. The counterweight rule below is not relaxed by the format; it is what makes the format honest.

AND THE LANGUAGE IS THE USER'S, NOT ENGLISH — Anthony, same exchange: "with agents able to understand multiple languages, the 'simple english' should be 'simple whatever_language_user_is_writing_in'." The plainness obligation is about REGISTER, not about English: no jargon, no ids, short sentences, in whatever language the user is writing in. cap:surface already says "in the user's WORDS", and this makes the wider reading explicit so nobody implements it as an English-only rule. Every English-language phrasing in these design notes is an example of the register, never a specification of the language.

WHAT IS MISSING TODAY, and it is an omission rather than a prohibition. `detect-and-ask` is explicit that the agent must "never invent an answer on their behalf", which is right and must not be weakened. But the skill says nothing about offering a reading, so the default behaviour is a bare question — `gap_to_prompt` returns "is it covered, deferred, or dropped?" and the agent relays it. `cap:surface` ("turn a gap into a question in the user's words", `verified`) delivers the translation and nothing more.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT NEUTRALITY. `req:no-se-knowledge` says the user never needs systems engineering. A bare gap question hands them back the analysis the agent has already done and asks them to redo it in their own head — which is precisely the SE work that requirement exists to spare them. The agent has read the graph, seen the precedents, and formed a view; withholding it is not impartiality, it is making the user pay for the agent's caution.

IT IS ALSO WHAT `dec:three-party-checks` ALREADY DESCRIBES: "The LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides." Offering a reading IS the LLM speaking. The decision stays with the human, untouched — and `dec:certainty-derived` still governs the write, because a recommendation changes no status until the user answers.

THE LINE THAT MUST NOT BE CROSSED, stated so this cannot be read as licence. Recommending is not deciding: no requirement moves off `proposed`, no decision reaches `accepted`, no gap is acknowledged on a reading the user has not confirmed. And a recommendation must carry WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT — the condition under which the other option wins — or it is steering rather than advising. An option presented without its counterweight is a decision taken quietly.

THE PART WORTH RECORDING, and the reason this is design rather than style: WHEN THE USER OVERRULES A RECOMMENDATION, THAT IS INFORMATION. A design where the agent advised one way and the human chose another has learned something neither party knew alone, and today it is invisible because the recommendation was never on the record. Whether the recommendation itself should be stored beside the question is left open here rather than assumed. NOTE that obligation (2) sharpens this: marking the recommendation is what makes an overrule an identifiable EVENT rather than an unremarkable choice among equals.

MEASURED, not theorised: every gap put to Anthony on 2026-07-31 needed the recommendation added by hand, and he asked for it explicitly TWICE that day — "provide your recommendation", "present them in simple english and your recommendations for how to proceed" — and a THIRD time in the same session, at which point he asked for the behaviour to be cemented rather than repeated. A shape a user has to request each time is a default in the wrong place. This requirement's own evidence therefore accumulated by the exact mechanism it describes.

SCOPE, stated because the third request widened it: this began as a rule about GAPS, and Anthony's framing — "the decisions I need to make" — is broader. The obligation is read as covering any point where the agent puts a CHOICE to the user, not only where detect_gaps produced it. Whether that widening needs its own capability rather than riding this one is left open rather than assumed.

TENSION NAMED SO IT IS NOT CONFLATED: `dec:report-dont-judge` says the confirmation ledger reports claim history and never judges a claim. That governs what a COMPUTATION may assert about evidence. It does not govern whether an agent may advise a human who asked — different actor, different act. Conflating the two would silence exactly the party `dec:three-party-checks` puts there to speak.
